# 1 Maccabees Chapter 10 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_010_page_001.jpg

---

**1** In the one hundred and sixtieth year Alexander Epiphanes, son of Antiochus, came up and seized Ptolemais; they received him, and he established himself as king there.

**2** When King Demetrius heard of it, he assembled a very large army and marched out to meet him in battle.

**3** Demetrius sent a letter to Jonathan with conciliatory words, designed to honor him.

**4** For Demetrius said: "We must act before Alexander makes peace with the Jews before we do and they side against us;

**5** for he will remember all the wrongs we did against him, his brothers, and his people."

**6** He granted Jonathan authority to raise troops and produce weapons, declaring him the king's ally, and ordered that the hostages in the citadel be released to him.

**7** Jonathan came to Jerusalem and read the letters aloud to all the people and to those in the citadel.

**8** They were greatly afraid when they heard that the king had given Jonathan authority to raise an army.

**9** The garrison in the citadel released the hostages to Jonathan, and he returned them to their families.

**10** Jonathan settled in Jerusalem and set about rebuilding and restoring the city.

**11** He directed those doing the work to build the walls and Mount Zion round about with dressed stone for fortification, and they did so.

**12** The foreigners who occupied the strongholds that Bacchides had built took flight;

**13** each of them abandoned his post and returned to his own land.

**14** Only in Beth-zur did some men who had forsaken the law and the commandments remain, for it served as their refuge.

**15** Alexander the king heard of all the promises that Demetrius had made to Jonathan; he was also told of the battles Jonathan and his brothers had fought and the hardships they had endured.

**16** He said: "Shall we ever find another man like him? We must make him our friend and ally now."

**17** He wrote him a letter, which read as follows:

**18** "King Alexander to his brother Jonathan, greetings.

**19** We have heard of you — that you are a mighty warrior and deserving to be our friend.

**20** We appoint you today as high priest of your nation, and you shall be called the King's Friend — and he sent him a purple robe and a gold crown — and you shall side with us and maintain friendship with us."

**21** Jonathan put on the sacred vestments in the seventh month of the one hundred and sixtieth year, at the Feast of Tabernacles; he also raised troops and equipped them with arms in abundance.

**22** When Demetrius heard of these things, he was distressed and said:

**23** "Why have we let Alexander outmaneuver us in winning the friendship of the Jews, which is a source of support?

**24** I will write them encouraging words as well, offer them honor and gifts, so that they will stand with me."

**25** He sent them a letter in these words: "King Demetrius to the Jewish nation, greetings.

**26** Since you have kept your covenants with us and remained in our friendship, refusing to side with our enemies, we have learned of this and rejoice.

**27** Continue, therefore, to keep faith with us, and we will generously reward you for all you do on our behalf.

**28** We will grant you many exemptions and will give you gifts.

**29** Now I hereby free you and exempt all Jews from tribute, from the salt tax, and from the crown levies.

**30** And in place of collecting one-third of the grain harvest and half the fruit of trees — what is due me by right — I hereby release you from this, from today onward and forever. I will not collect this from the land of Judea or from the three districts annexed from Samaria and Galilee, from this day and for all time.

**31** Jerusalem and all its territory shall be holy and exempt from taxation.

**32** I also surrender my authority over the citadel in Jerusalem and give it to the high priest, to garrison with such men as he shall select.

**33** Every Jew who has been taken captive from the land of Judea anywhere in my kingdom I release without ransom; let all their taxes be remitted, including taxes on their livestock.

**34** All feasts, Sabbaths, new moons, and appointed days — and the three days before and after each feast — shall be days of immunity and freedom for all Jews within my kingdom.

**35** No one shall have power to exact payment from them or to molest them in any matter.

**36** Let thirty thousand Jews be enrolled in the royal forces, with allowances equal to all royal troops; let some of them be stationed in the great royal fortresses,

**37** and let some be appointed to positions of trust in the kingdom. Let their officers and leaders come from their own ranks, and let them follow their own customs, as the king has decreed for the land of Judea.

**38** The three districts added to Judea from the country of Samaria — let them be incorporated into Judea and placed under a single authority, that of the high priest, not subject to any other authority.

**39** Ptolemais and its surrounding territory I give as an endowment to the Jerusalem sanctuary for its necessary expenses.

**40** I also give fifteen thousand shekels of silver annually from the royal revenues, from the appropriate accounts.

**41** All the surplus that the officials have not paid in past years, as required, shall henceforth be paid into the temple treasury.

**42** Moreover, the five thousand shekels of silver that were taken annually from the temple income shall be released; these belong to the priests who serve there.

**43** Anyone who takes refuge in the temple at Jerusalem or anywhere within its precinct, whether in debt or under any liability — they shall be set free, and all their property in my kingdom shall be released.

**44** The expense of building and renovating the works of the sanctuary shall be paid from the royal revenues.

**45** The cost of building the walls of Jerusalem and of its complete fortification, and the cost of fortifying the walls in Judea — these too shall come from the royal revenues."

**46** When Jonathan and the people heard these words, they put no stock in them and did not accept them, because they remembered the great wrong Demetrius had done to Israel and the severe suffering he had caused.

**47** They were pleased with Alexander because he had been the first to propose peace, and they remained his allies for the rest of his days.

**48** King Alexander assembled a large army and took up a position opposite Demetrius.

**49** The two kings engaged in battle; the army of Demetrius fled, and Alexander pursued them and defeated them.

**50** The battle raged until sunset; Demetrius fell on that day.

**51** Alexander sent envoys to King Ptolemy of Egypt with the following message:

**52** "Since I have returned to my kingdom, taken my seat on the throne of my fathers, gained control of the land, and crushed Demetrius —

**53** for I engaged him in battle and both he and his army were defeated by us, so that we now occupy his royal throne —

**54** let us now establish friendship between us. Give me your daughter now as wife; I will be your son-in-law and give gifts to you and to her worthy of you."

**55** King Ptolemy replied: "Blessed be the day on which you returned to the land of your fathers and took the throne of their kingdom.

**56** I will do as you have proposed. Come to meet me at Ptolemais, so that we may see one another, and I will become your father-in-law, as you have said."

**57** Ptolemy set out from Egypt with his daughter Cleopatra and arrived at Ptolemais in the one hundred and sixty-second year.

**58** King Alexander met him there, and he gave him his daughter Cleopatra. Their wedding was celebrated at Ptolemais with great splendor, as kings customarily do.

**59** King Alexander wrote to Jonathan to come and meet him.

**60** Jonathan went in state to Ptolemais and met both kings; he presented them and their courtiers with silver, gold, and many gifts, and won their favor.

**61** A company of scoundrels from Israel, troublemakers, had gathered to bring accusations against him, but the king paid them no attention.

**62** The king gave orders that Jonathan's clothing be removed and that he be dressed in purple; this was done.

**63** The king seated him at his side and said to his commanders: "Go with him into the center of the city and announce that no one shall bring charges against him about any matter, and no one shall trouble him for any reason."

**64** When his accusers saw the honor accorded him, as announced, and saw him clothed in purple, they all fled.

**65** The king conferred honor on him, enrolled him among his chief friends, and appointed him general and governor of the province.

**66** Jonathan returned to Jerusalem in peace and gladness.

**67** In the one hundred and sixty-fifth year Demetrius the son of Demetrius came over from Crete to the land of his ancestors.

**68** When King Alexander heard of it, he was deeply troubled and returned to Antioch.

**69** Demetrius appointed Apollonius as governor of Coele-Syria. Apollonius assembled a large army and encamped at Jamnia, sending this message to Jonathan the high priest:

**70** "You alone defy us, and I have become an object of ridicule and mockery because of you. Why do you exert authority over us in the hill country?

**71** If you trust your troops, come down to us in the plain and let us settle things there, for the power of cities is with me.

**72** Inquire and learn who I am and who my allies are; they will tell you that you cannot hold out against us, since your ancestors were twice driven to flight in their own land.

**73** And now you will not be able to withstand cavalry and a force this size on the plain, where there is no stone, no rock, no place to retreat."

**74** When Jonathan heard these words of Apollonius, his spirit was stirred; he chose ten thousand men, marched out from Jerusalem, and his brother Simon came to support him.

**75** He camped against Joppa, but the men of the city shut him out, because Apollonius had a garrison there. He attacked the city.

**76** The men of the city were frightened and opened the gates, and Jonathan captured Joppa.

**77** When Apollonius heard, he mustered three thousand cavalry and a large infantry force and marched to Azotus as if passing through, while actually advancing into the plain, relying on his large cavalry contingent.

**78** Jonathan pursued him as far as Azotus and the two armies engaged.

**79** But Apollonius had secretly left one thousand cavalry in their rear.

**80** Jonathan discovered that there was an ambush behind him; his army was surrounded and pelted with arrows from morning till evening.

**81** But the troops held their ground as Jonathan had commanded, while the enemy horses wore themselves out.

**82** Then Simon brought his force forward and engaged the phalanx, for the cavalry was exhausted; they broke before him and fled.

**83** The cavalry scattered across the plain; they fled to Azotus and entered the temple of Dagon — their idol — seeking safety.

**84** Jonathan set fire to Azotus and the surrounding towns and seized their plunder; the temple of Dagon and those who had taken refuge in it he burned to the ground.

**85** Those killed in battle, together with those burned, came to about eight thousand men.

**86** From there Jonathan marched and encamped before Ashkelon, and the men of the city came out to meet him with great ceremony.

**87** Jonathan and those with him returned to Jerusalem with rich spoils.

**88** When King Alexander heard of these things, he honored Jonathan still more,

**89** and sent him a golden clasp, of the kind given to the king's kinsmen, and granted him Ekron and all its territory as a possession.
